seoDescription:
RES is hiring a Lead Estimator for high-voltage substations and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects. Based remotely, this role prepares detailed cost estimates for utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure, including substation construction up to 500kV, transmission components, and battery storage facilities. You will lead a team of estimators, manage complex multi-phase proposals, and coordinate with preconstruction managers and engineering teams on EPC (Engineer-Procure-Construct) and design-build projects.

Responsibilities

  • Prepare cost estimates for utility-grade substation, high-voltage transmission, and BESS projects, incorporating labor, material, equipment, and productivity factors
  • Lead and oversee multiple estimators on concurrent project proposals for Bid-Build and EPC construction RFPs
  • Review RFP documents to identify project scope, pricing elements, and technical requirements
  • Complete quantity take-offs from construction plans and design documents for substation systems up to 500kV
  • Compile indicative budgets in the absence of fully engineered documents
  • Manage vendor and subcontractor quote requests; evaluate responses for accuracy and schedule compliance
  • Coordinate with preconstruction managers on engineering support services and project schedule alignment
  • Maintain and apply current market data for construction, material, and soft costs; assess impacts from local labor, commodity pricing, and client specifications
  • Identify and document project risks in risk registers
  • Create bid proposal documents including Statements of Value (SOV), technical forms, and Assumptions/Clarifications/Exclusions (ACE) documents
  • Present project scope, risks, and cost estimates to operations and executive leadership
  • Collaborate with proposal strategists and preconstruction managers on final RFP responses
  • Compile and maintain historical cost data for project analysis

Requirements

  • Associate's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related field; OR high school diploma with 2+ years equivalent industry experience
  • 7+ years hands-on estimating experience for substation and high-voltage systems
  • 1+ year field-based construction experience
  • 2+ years leading a team of estimators on project pursuits or supervisory experience (preferred)
  • 2+ years estimating BESS DC and AC coupled systems (preferred)
  • Extensive experience with EPC and Balance of Plant (BOP) estimate structures for utility-scale renewable energy projects
  • Knowledge of design-build construction methods and production-based cost estimation
  • Ability to complete quantity take-offs from construction plans and geotechnical reports
  • Proficiency with Blue Beam or Adobe for quantity take-off work
  • Experience with HCSS HeavyBid or similar estimating software
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Excel, Word, Project, OneNote, Teams, and SharePoint
  • Ability to evaluate site conditions and develop competitive estimates based on labor, equipment, and material resources
  • Ability to travel 5–15% as required
  • Pre-employment background check and drug screening required

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Health Savings Account with employer contribution
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 4× salary basic life insurance and voluntary life insurance
  • Short- and long-term disability coverage
  • Accident, hospital, and critical illness insurance
  • 401(k) plan with 6% company match
  • 4 weeks paid time off and 10 paid holidays
  • Tuition reimbursement and green car reimbursement
  • Volunteer and charity matching
  • Paid parental leave and paid sabbatical leave
  • Employee referral bonus
  • Employee discounts and wellness programs
  • Wellness reimbursement
  • Position is bonus eligible
  • Salary range: $142,000–$178,000 based on education, qualifications, experience, and location

seoDescription:
Enphase Energy seeks a Field Service Technician for its Massachusetts, MA territory. The role provides on-site support to distribution and installation partners for PV and storage systems. Regular travel of up to 50 percent is required, including out-of-state trips, overnight stays, and assignments of up to two consecutive weeks.

Responsibilities

  • Service Enphase PV and storage systems within the assigned territory.
  • Coordinate site visits with the scheduling team and homeowners to align Enphase Customer Support with system owners.
  • Perform onsite testing and diagnostics to evaluate system performance and identify issues.
  • Work on rooftops and elevated structures on a regular basis.
  • Complete solar maintenance reports and required documentation accurately and on time.
  • Perform microinverter maintenance and update the Enlighten monitoring system to reflect changes.
  • Use standard field tools including drills, levels, squares, tape measures, and ladders.
  • Install and route conduit, copper piping, and flexible tubing; pull and manage wiring as needed.
  • Participate in regular safety training and follow all company safety protocols.
  • Maintain tool inventory according to company standards.
  • Follow OSHA safety standards on all job sites.
  • Train and mentor team members on installation techniques and best practices.
  • Review system designs and develop job-specific bills of materials.
  • Meet domestic travel requirements including valid identification for air travel.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • 2+ years of experience in electrical installation and service.
  • Valid state driver’s license with a clean driving record and insurability.
  • Proficiency with computers and multiple applications, including Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Ability to read and interpret plan sets.
  • Commercial or residential electrical license.
  • NABCEP certification.
  • Ability to work outside regular business hours as needed.
  • Ability to regularly lift and move up to 60 pounds of tools and equipment.
  • Frequent use of hands to handle, grasp, and reach.
  • Safe and effective operation of hand and power tools.
  • Frequent standing, walking, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling.
  • Ascend and descend ladders as required.
  • Work on rooftops, uneven surfaces, heights, and confined spaces.
  • Work outdoors in various weather conditions and around electrical hazards.

Benefits

  • Hourly rate range of $23 to $36, varying by experience, skills, and location.
  • Eligibility for bonus, equity, and benefits, with final compensation determined by applicable laws and internal equity.

seoDescription:
The Construction Project Manager role at RES is a site-based position managing utility-scale EPC projects from start to finish. Primary location is Houston, Texas, with additional sites in Phoenix, Arizona; Waco, Texas; and Little Rock, Arkansas. The position requires full ownership of project performance, including safety, quality, schedule, budget, contract administration, and client deliverables, with 76-100% travel expected.

Responsibilities

  • Manage the HSE plan and ensure processes align with project requirements.
  • Oversee client relationships, report project status and forecasts to stakeholders, and address concerns on schedule.
  • Lead development and updates of the Project Execution Plan, including kickoff, close-out meetings, and construction permits.
  • Collaborate on Level 3 schedules, identify and manage critical path activities, and coordinate with the Project Superintendent on EPC delivery.
  • Track costs, allocate budget, forecast to completion, and manage procurement, subcontracts, and materials for profit improvement.
  • Maintain understanding of contractual obligations, document changes, ensure flow-down to vendors, and manage change orders with required approvals and documentation.
  • Drive risk management plans, implement preventive and corrective measures, and support timely decisions.
  • Review and approve quality management plans and ITPs, track non-conformances in Procore, and close NCRs with cost documentation.
  • Provide documents for EMS monitoring, support permitting, and ensure field staff maintain required certifications.
  • Utilize SMS, QMS, EMS, and technical procedures; perform audits for compliance.
  • Operate company vehicle safely in all conditions and commit to short- or long-term remote site assignments.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Project Management, or Construction Management, or equivalent experience where 2 years of work experience equals 1 year of education.
  • 4 or more years of EPC Project Management experience.
  • 3 or more years of Solar or T&D EPC experience.
  • Valid driver’s license.
  • Advanced knowledge of project management best practices, estimating, change orders, project permits, QA/QC processes, project finance, contract management, sub-contractor and materials management, construction drawing review, quantity takeoff, engineering management, Microsoft Office suite, scheduling software (MS Project, Primavera 6), and job costing or accounting software.
  • Ability to travel 76-100% of the time and commit to short- or long-term remote site assignments.
  • Rarely required: climbing, crouching, kneeling, pulling/pushing/lifting 5-15 lbs., stooping.
  • Occasionally required: carrying 5-15 lbs., gripping, handling, pinching, walking; exposure to noise and hazards.
  • Frequently required: standing.
  • Constantly required: reading, grasping, hearing, reaching, vision, repetitive motion, sitting.
  • Rarely exposed to extreme cold, heat, humidity, or wet climates.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage; health savings account with employer contribution; flexible spending accounts.
  • 4x pay basic life and voluntary life; short- and long-term disability; accident, hospital, and critical illness coverage.
  • 401(k) plan with 6% company match.
  • 4 weeks PTO and 10 paid holidays.
  • Tuition reimbursement, green car reimbursement, volunteer and charity matching.
  • Paid parental leave and paid sabbatical leave.
  • Employee referral bonus, employee discounts, wellness programs, and wellness reimbursement.
  • Base salary range $122,000–$153,000; position is bonus eligible; final compensation based on education, qualifications, experience, and work location.

                                                    Denver, Colorado

We are committed to building a workplace where everyone feels heard and respected, and extending our culture of care so that every individual can reach their full potential. We want you to have a sense of belonging and feel valued for your contributions and the perspectives you bring.

\u00A0

Summary:\u00A0

The Sr. Engineer IV - Solar Engineering provides solar PV performance and design expertise on utility-scale solar and solar plus storage projects during the development, design, construction, and commissioning phases.

\u00A0

This role will be hybrid requiring a minimum of 3 days in office.

\u00A0

Requirements:\u00A0\u00A0\u00A0

  • Serves as a lead Solar Engineering subject matter expert for internal departments, including development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and engineering (civil, electrical, SCADA, and engineering delivery).
  • Leads the evaluation and resolution of complex technical issues with clients, developers, engineers, procurement, subcontractors, and construction. Communicates material risks and recommendations to leadership.
  • Drafts, reviews, and approves contracts, exhibits, scopes of work, and technical documentation related to design, energy yields, commissioning, testing, and performance.
  • Leads analysis of plant and equipment performance using SCADA, MET, inverter, tracker, meter, and DC collection data to identify underperformance, data-quality issues, and likely root causes.
  • Develops and maintains engineering data structures, equipment hierarchies, mappings, and validation workflows that connect design, commissioning, SCADA, and performance information.
  • Leads technical roles with clients, internal leadership, and procurement on technical items that inform commercial design decisions related to risk management.
  • Coordinates engineering priorities, assignments, subconsultant activities, and progress to maintain project schedules, quality requirements, and conformance with contract documents. Leads technical feedback to clients and subcontractors based on the review of external design documentation, including design basis, overall site plans, energy models, contractual exhibits, and performance test results.
  • Works closely with clients and construction teams to guarantee delivery of a quality PV system that meets contractual expectations.
  • Generates and responds to design RFIs related to design and project performance.
  • Leads the creation and continuous improvement of team templates, tools, processes, scripts, calculators, visualizations, technical specifications, analysis methodologies, test procedures, and standardization and automation of workflows.
  • Provides leadership, coaching, and mentoring to the solar engineering team.
  • Coordinates with Development on preliminary layouts, technology assessments, and basis of design. Drafts, reviews, and approves standard processes that impact team templates and workflow.
  • Attends work regularly and punctually, as scheduled or expected.
  • Complies with Employee Handbook, Code of Conduct, and Company Policies & Procedures.

\u00A0

Additional Responsibilities:

  • Presents, supports, and leads-by-example with a safety and quality-oriented attitude.
  • Provides support to construction during the construction and commissioning phases.
  • Reviews work instructions periodically to ensure compliance with industry and client standards.
  • Develops new methods and standards for Group design activities.

Safety:

  • Follows safety and security procedures and determines appropriate action.\u00A0 Reports potentially unsafe conditions and uses materials and equipment properly.

\u00A0Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field of study required. Master\u2019s degree preferred.
  • 8 or more years of progressive experience, including utility-scale PV engineering and technical expertise related to site feasibility, energy modeling, major equipment selection, and site layout is required.
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally 5 to 15% required.
  • Must possess a valid Driver\u2019s license.\u00A0
  • Strong oral and written skills.
  • Technical writing: Drafting reports, papers, and assessments to a high standard
  • Ability to communicate issues and to communicate complex technical issues to peers across internal departments, suppliers and clients, and a non-technical audience as required.
  • Clear and concise writing.
  • Negotiation skills.
  • Interpersonal skills, including the ability to work well in a team environment.
  • Ability to organize and prioritize work. Project management and time management skills, including balancing multiple Projects under tight deadlines and establishing and maintaining good relations with internal team members and clients.
  • Ability to think analytically.
  • Advanced /Expert level Knowledge in:
  • PV plant performance analysis, energy modeling, expected-versus-actual evaluation, uncertainty analysis, and regression methods.
  • Engineering review of equipment hierarchies, design drawings, SCADA tags, data mappings, and large time-series datasets to support performance diagnostics and project decision-making.
  • PV Plant Capacity and Operational Testing\u00A0
  • National and international codes and standards applicable to PV design, construction, commissioning, and testing, including NEC, NFPA, ASTM, IEC, IBC, ASCE, and NETA requirements. PV Electrical Design\u00A0
  • Design for Constructability
  • Installation and Application
  • Solar Industry best practices
  • Major equipment specification, selection, and application, including modules, inverters, trackers, MET stations, meters, SCADA systems, and DC collection equipment.
  • Ability to lead the team members and advise clients regarding performance analysis, solar Project design/development, module/inverter/tracking system technology selection.
  • Ability to lead the team on risks and opportunities for incorporating new technologies into PV designs and performance modeling.
  • Experience with Design Software:
  • Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D
  • PV simulation software PVsyst,SAM, PVfarm, and Solar Resource Compass
  • Global Mapper or GIS software
  • Python-based data analysis and automation, including processing, validating, visualizing, and reporting large engineering and time-series datasets.Statistics including uncertainty analysis and regression models.
  • MS Office (Excel, Word, Outlook, etc.)\u00A0
  • Functional competencies include accountability, attention to detail, customer focus, prioritization, and continuous improvement.

\u00A0

\u00A0

Anticipated base salary range:\u00A0 $127,000 \u2013 $158,000

\u00A0

The final agreed upon compensation is based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. This position is bonus eligible.

\u00A0

RES offers benefits that are effective first day of employment. These benefits include the following:

\u00A0

  • Medical, Dental and Vision
  • Health Savings Account with employer contribution
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 4x pay Basic Life and Voluntary Life
  • Short and Long Term Disability
  • Accident, Hospital, and Critical Illness
  • 401 (k) plan with 6% company match
  • 4 weeks Paid Time Off (PTO) and 10 Paid Holidays
  • Tuition Reimbursement and Green Car Reimbursement
  • Volunteer and Charity Matching
  • Paid Parental Leave and Paid Sabbatical Leave

  • Wellness Reimbursement

Summary:\u00A0

The Electrical Engineer III \u2013 Electrical Engineering\u00A0provides engineering / conceptual and detailed designs of utility-scale renewable power plants (wind & solar) and battery storage systems.\u00A0 Aids in operations support renewable power generation projects; while supporting the development, engineering, and construction of projects.

\u00A0

Requirements:\u00A0\u00A0\u00A0

  • Develops and reviews the preliminary and detailed design of AC (Low, Medium, and High Voltage) and DC systems, including DC power blocks (PV) and MV AC collection systems (PV/Wind).
  • Develops models of the AC substation and collection systems and performs and reviews Load Flow and Short Circuit analyses, DC and AC loss calculations, cable ampacity studies, and AC/DC cable sizing.

  • Prepares and reviews specifications and construction documents to identify design and performance requirements for procurement of electrical materials and equipment.
  • Performs technical review of proposed equipment to ensure acceptability to company, client, and industry standards.
  • Works with designers to develop and review construction drawings and documentation to communicate electrical installation details effectively to construction teams.
  • Provides input to team members working on other project areas, including grounding system design, substation design, and medium voltage collection system design.
  • Prepares and analyzes weekly project updates for electrical engineering design progress for project management.
  • Performs assignment and progress tracking of tasks for team members and sub-consultants.
  • Attends work regularly and punctually, as scheduled or expected.
  • Complies with Employee Handbook, Code of Conduct, and Company Policies & Procedures.
  • Presents, supports, and leads-by-example with a safety and quality-oriented attitude.
  • Provides support to construction during the construction and commissioning phases.
  • Reviews work instructions periodically to ensure compliance with industry and client standards.
  • Develops new methods and standards for Group design activities.
  • Visits sites as needed during pre-construction and construction to support project needs.

\u00A0

Safety:

  • Follows safety and security procedures and determines appropriate action.\u00A0 Reports potentially unsafe conditions and uses materials and equipment properly.

\u00A0

Qualifications:

  • Bachelors degree in Electrical Engineering or 8 years equivalent experience is required.
  • Professional Engineer (PE or P. Eng.) certification is required.
  • Masters degree in Electrical Engineering is preferred.
  • 5+ years of power generation industry with EPC experience is required.
  • Ability to travel 5-15%.
  • A valid drivers license is required.
  • Advanced level of knowledge in:
    • Power Systems Analysis, load flow, and short circuit modeling
    • Reactive compensation evaluation\u00A0
    • DC and AC Electrical Design\u00A0
    • Design for Constructability
    • US and Canadian Industry Standards
    • Preparation of Equipment Specifications
    • Oral and written skills include:
      • Clear and concise technical writing
      • Ability to communicate issues internally with Electrical, Solar, Civil/Structural, and Mechanical Engineers, CAD Designers, Project Managers, and Contract and Estimating Teams and Externally with Clients and suppliers\u00A0
  • Intermediate level of knowledge in:
    • Medium to High Voltage Substation Design\u00A0
    • Transmission Line Design Concepts
    • Grounding System Design Concepts
    • Project Scheduling Concepts
    • Detailed Design Software:\u00A0
      • MathCAD\u00A0
      • Fundamental understanding of CAD concepts
      • Fundamental knowledge of power system software such as DIgSILENT, SKM, and ETAP\u00A0
      • Basic understanding of grounding software like WinIGS or CDEGS
      • Knowledge of Dynamic Modeling Software such as PSS/E
  • MS Office (Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams)\u00A0
  • Strong interpersonal skills, including listening and summarizing skills
  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills
  • Must have a valid current driver license, eligible for corporate vehicle insurance coverage.
  • Functional competencies include attention to detail, excellence, prioritization, teamwork, and continuous improvement

\u00A0

Anticipated base salary range:\u00A0 $110,000 - $139,000

\u00A0

The final agreed upon compensation is based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. This position is bonus eligible.

\u00A0

RES offers benefits that are effective first day of employment. These benefits include the following:

\u00A0

  • Medical, Dental and Vision
  • Health Savings Account with employer contribution
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 4x pay Basic Life and Voluntary Life
  • Short and Long Term Disability
  • Accident, Hospital, and Critical Illness
  • 401 (k) plan with 6% company match
  • 4 weeks Paid Time Off (PTO) and 10 Paid Holidays
  • Tuition Reimbursement and Green Car Reimbursement
  • Volunteer and Charity Matching
  • Paid Parental Leave and Paid Sabbatical Leave
  • Employee Referral Bonus
  • Employee Discounts and Wellness programs
  • Wellness Reimbursement

\u00A0

Physical requirements and environment:

\u00A0

The work environment and physical demands characteristics are representative of those the employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.\u00A0 Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

\u00A0

Occasionally exposed to noise and hazards in the work environment.

\u00A0

\u00A0

RES is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. Tired of the status quo? So are we. Freedom Power is leading the charge in the rapidly expanding world of home electrification. We’ve unified the expertise of Freedom Solar and Freedom HVAC to become a complete whole-house energy provider, and we're looking for passionate individuals to join our unstoppable team. If you want to build a rewarding career by helping homeowners take control of their energy, slash their bills, and stay protected no matter what—your future starts here.

Pride in Quality Craftsmanship 
Go Above and Beyond 
Put People First 
Have a Humble Heart 
Give a Damn 
Shoot Straight 



Job Summary: Freedom Solar Power is looking for dedicated, humble, and hardworking Commercial Solar Installers for national commercial solar-based projects with either construction, electrical or solar experience! You will join a crew of solar installers to install 10kW to 1MW solar systems. This position is 90% travel; mostly 4 weeks out, with occasional weekend travel/work required.
 
THIS TRAVELING INSTALLER ROLE IS BASED OUT OF AUSTIN, TX.
seoDescription:
Freedom Solar Power seeks Commercial Solar Installers to deploy photovoltaic systems on commercial projects across the United States. Based in Austin, TX, this role involves extensive travel—approximately 90% of the time, typically in 4-week assignments with occasional weekend commitments.

About the Role

You will install commercial-scale solar PV systems ranging from 10kW to 1MW capacity as part of dedicated installation crews. This position requires significant on-site presence at project locations nationwide.

Responsibilities

  • Install photovoltaic modules, racking systems, and electrical components on commercial rooftop and ground-mount installations
  • Perform DC and AC wiring for solar arrays and interconnection points
  • Work collaboratively with crew members to meet project timelines and safety standards
  • Maintain tools and equipment in working condition
  • Follow blueprints, engineering specifications, and installation best practices

Requirements

  • Prior experience in construction, electrical work, or solar installation
  • Physical ability to work at heights, lift heavy materials, and perform manual labor in outdoor conditions
  • Willingness to travel extensively and work away from home for multi-week periods
  • Ability to work weekends when project schedules require
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Benefits

Freedom Solar Power provides competitive compensation and the opportunity to work on large-scale energy infrastructure projects with a Texas-based company operating nationwide.

title: Licensed Solar Electrician -Residential Wireman/Journeyman
description:
Solar Electricians Who Mean Business: This One’s for You
Austin, TX   Full-Time   On-Site
Some jobs pull wire. This one powers an entire revolution — and puts you at the center of it.
Freedom Power was born when Freedom Solar and Freedom HVAC joined forces to become Texas's complete whole-house energy company. We don't just install solar panels. We hand homeowners the keys to something bigger: control over their energy, their bills, and their future. We call it Energy Empowerment, and it's not a tagline — it's the reason we show up every day.
If you've got electrical mastery in your hands and hustle in your blood, this is your shot to do more than run conduit. You'll walk into homes as a skilled technician, execute precise solar electrical installations, upgrade service panels, and bring whole-home energy systems to life. Solar, batteries, generators — you'll be the hands-on expert making Energy Empowerment real, one installation at a time. Every job is local, and you'll roll in your own company truck.
Competitive pay and performance bonuses on top.
What You'll Do
Install electrical equipment and circuits, complete DC conduit runs, and interconnect PV systems to existing residential services.
Upgrade customer electrical service as needed — main panel upgrades and meter bases, external disconnects, and code compliance assessments.
Perform system testing — voltage, amperage, and power tests for each installation.
Complete commissioning and inspection checklists with precision.
Follow and enforce safety procedures and protocols on every job site.

description:
About Us
 
Solar Landscape is the leading commercial rooftop solar developer in the U.S. Only 4% of commercial rooftops host solar today — we’re changing that, fast. Commercial rooftop solar is the fastest, smartest way to build new clean power — delivering megawatts of generation in months, not years, and powering America’s energy and future right where it’s needed most. By turning rooftops into local power plants, we’re reshaping how — and how fast — energy gets built in the U.S.
 
Recognized as the #1 Distributed Generation Developer by New Project Media, the #1 National Commercial Rooftop Solar Developer by Solar Power World, and winner of the U.S. Department of Energy’s Grand Prize for Clean Energy, Solar Landscape is defining the future of energy generation in America.
 
Headquartered in Asbury Park, New Jersey, Solar Landscape has offices in Chicago, Baltimore, and New York City and operates in over a dozen states nationwide.
 
We move fast, solve hard problems, and take our work seriously — but never ourselves. We value clear thinking, accountability, and execution. At the same time, we’re collaborative by default, and believe the best work happens when people enjoy working together. Our team is made up of smart, grounded people who show up for each other — whether that’s troubleshooting a system design or catching up over lunch.
 
If you’re looking to do meaningful work in a high-performance environment — and be part of the team reshaping how energy gets built in the U.S. — we’d love to meet you.

Solar Installer. Powering Texas, One Rooftop at a Time.
Austin, TX   Full-Time   On-Site
Some jobs put panels on roofs. This one puts power in people's hands — and you're the one who makes it happen.
Freedom Power was born when Freedom Solar and Freedom HVAC joined forces to become Texas's complete whole-house energy company. We don't just install solar systems. We hand homeowners the keys to something bigger: control over their energy, their bills, and their future. We call it Energy Empowerment, and it's not a tagline — it's the reason we show up every day.
If you've got construction know-how in your hands and hustle in your blood, this is your shot to do work that actually matters. You'll be part of a tight crew installing 1kW–30kW solar systems on residential homes across Austin — racking, DC and AC equipment, commissioning, testing, all of it. No two rooftops are the same, and every system you bring online is one more family taking control of their energy future.
Competitive pay with performance bonuses on top.
What You'll Do
Attend daily safety meetings before any work is performed on-site — safety is non-negotiable.
Install racking systems per manufacturer specs and Freedom Solar plans across a variety of residential roof types.
Install DC and AC equipment per plans and local codes.
Commission and test PV systems safely, including voltage testing from 10V–1000VDC and 120V–480VAC.
Make field changes as needed and communicate clearly with the Project Manager.
Drive company trucks and trailers safely to and from job sites.
Support the crew lead and Regional Operations Manager with other duties as assigned.
What You Bring
Residential solar installation experience (required)
Valid driver's license and clean MVR — required to drive company vehicles
OSHA 10 required; OSHA 30 preferred
Apprentice Electrical License preferred
Electrical experience strongly recommended
Knowledge of local electrical codes and residential PV design and components
Ability to read blueprints, wiring schematics, and electrical instructions
Background in construction trades — roofing, carpentry, or metal framing is a plus
The Physical Side
Comfortable on rooftops, ladders, and at heights — every day
Able to lift 50–75+ lbs routinely throughout the day
Good with bending, stretching, squatting, and sustained physical effort
Unbothered by Texas heat (100°F+), cold snaps, or wet conditions — you work in all of it
What's In It For You
Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
100% Company-Sponsored Short-Term Disability
401(k) Employer Matching
Weekly Pay Dates
3 Weeks PTO + 3 Sick Days
12 Paid Holidays + 1 Floating Holiday
Upward mobility opportunities
One More Thing
One of our favorite core values is Give a Damn — and that's exactly what we're looking for. We hire for grit, craftsmanship, and character as much as resumes — and we're always excited to discover skills we didn't know we needed.
Freedom Power is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

title: Solar O&M Technician (Chicago)
description:
About Us
 
Solar Landscape is the leading commercial rooftop solar developer in the U.S. Only 4% of commercial rooftops host solar today — we’re changing that, fast. Commercial rooftop solar is the fastest, smartest way to build new clean power — delivering megawatts of generation in months, not years, and powering America’s energy and future right where it’s needed most. By turning rooftops into local power plants, we’re reshaping how — and how fast — energy gets built in the U.S.
 
Recognized as the #1 Distributed Generation Developer by New Project Media, the #1 National Commercial Rooftop Solar Developer by Solar Power World, and winner of the U.S. Department of Energy’s Grand Prize for Clean Energy, Solar Landscape is defining the future of energy generation in America.
 
Headquartered in Asbury Park, New Jersey, Solar Landscape has offices in Chicago, Baltimore, and New York City and operates in over a dozen states nationwide.
 
We move fast, solve hard problems, and take our work seriously — but never ourselves. We value clear thinking, accountability, and execution. At the same time, we’re collaborative by default, and believe the best work happens when people enjoy working together. Our team is made up of smart, grounded people who show up for each other — whether that’s troubleshooting a system design or catching up over lunch.
 
If you’re looking to do meaningful work in a high-performance environment — and be part of the team reshaping how energy gets built in the U.S. — we’d love to meet you.
 
About The Role


We are seeking O&M Technicians at multiple experience levels (Tier 1–4) to join our growing Operations & Management (O&M) team. These roles are critical to ensuring the reliable performance, safety, and efficiency of our commercial solar energy systems.
Whether you’re newer to the field or bring extensive solar experience, you’ll play an important role in maintaining, troubleshooting, and optimizing solar system performance while working in a collaborative, safety-focused environment.
seoDescription:
Solar Landscape, a leading commercial rooftop solar developer operating across the U.S., is hiring O&M Technicians at multiple experience levels (Tier 1–4) for its Chicago office. In this role, you will maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize the performance and safety of commercial solar energy systems, working within a growing operations team focused on reliable system delivery.

Responsibilities

  • Perform routine maintenance and inspections on commercial rooftop solar installations
  • Troubleshoot and diagnose system performance issues across DC/AC wiring, inverters, and monitoring equipment
  • Conduct preventive maintenance to ensure system reliability and efficiency
  • Monitor system performance data and respond to alerts or underperformance flags
  • Document maintenance activities and system conditions in company records
  • Support safe, compliant operation of solar energy systems

Requirements

  • Experience level requirements vary by tier; Tier 1 is entry-level; higher tiers require progressively more hands-on solar O&M or installation experience
  • Ability to work at heights and perform physical work on rooftops
  • Basic electrical knowledge and comfort with DC/AC systems
  • Valid driver's license

Benefits

  • Collaborative, safety-focused work environment
  • Opportunity to work on utility-scale commercial solar systems
  • Clear career progression through tier-based advancement

description:

Orlando, FL |  Full-Time  |  Hourly, Non-Exempt  |  Regional Travel
A solar system stops making sense the moment it stops making power. When that call comes in, you're the one who shows up, figures out what's wrong, and fixes it — on the spot.
Freedom Power was born when Freedom Solar and Freedom HVAC joined forces to become Texas and Florida's complete whole-house energy company. We don't just install equipment. We hand homeowners the keys to something bigger: control over their energy, their bills, and their future. We call it Energy Empowerment, and it's not a tagline — it's the reason we show up every day.
As a Solar Field Service Technician, you're the technical expert who keeps residential solar, storage, and off-grid systems running the way they're supposed to. You'll respond to dispatch calls, troubleshoot and diagnose issues, climb the roof when the job calls for it, and walk homeowners through exactly what you found and why — building trust one service call at a time.
Your Day-to-Day
Respond to service calls from dispatch on behalf of customers with solar system issues.
Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair Solar, storage, and off-grid systems.
Get on roofs when needed to remove, replace, or repair solar panels.
Deliver an exceptional customer experience on every visit.
Communicate findings clearly and follow procedures with your manager.
Handle paperwork, timekeeping, and inventory processing for every service call.
Collect payment for services rendered and identify legitimate upsell opportunities in the field.
Complete the job disposition form after every service call.
Take on other duties as assigned by the Service Operations Manager.
 
What You Bring
Prior solar installation experience
OSHA 10 certification (required)
Valid driver's license and willingness to travel regionally, frequently
Solid knowledge of local electrical codes and residential PV design and components
Strong understanding of residential AC (microinverters) and DC (string & optimizer) PV systems
Thorough understanding of residential electrical systems and how to work safely around them
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, safely
Comfortable learning new technical and diagnostic skills as systems evolve
Able to withstand heights, climb ladders, and work outdoors in hot and cold conditions
The Physical Side
Comfortable with light lifting and carrying (under 15 lbs), straight pulling, and simple grasping
Able to walk, stand, and sit for extended periods
Comfortable operating office equipment and motor vehicles, with travel by car up to 10% of the time
Able to work independently as well as with others

title: HVAC Maintenance Technician
description:
HVAC Maintenance Technician – Trusted Advisor
Houston, TX    Full-Time    On-Site
Anybody can run a checklist. We're looking for someone who can walk into a home, tell a family the truth about their system, and earn their trust before they even ask for it.
Freedom Power was born when Freedom Solar and Freedom HVAC joined forces to become Texas's complete whole-house energy company. We don't just install equipment. We hand homeowners the keys to something bigger: control over their energy, their bills, and their future. We call it Energy Empowerment, and it's not a tagline — it's the reason we show up every day.
As an HVAC Maintenance Technician, you're the reason our customers sleep easy. You'll run thorough preventative maintenance visits, catch the small problems before they become expensive ones, and explain exactly what you find — no pressure, no scare tactics, just facts and photos. When a repair or upgrade genuinely makes sense, you'll be the one homeowners trust to tell them so.
Your Day-to-Day
Perform scheduled preventative maintenance on residential HVAC systems, top to bottom.
Run comprehensive inspections using our maintenance checklists — condensers, coils, blower components, drain systems, electrical, capacitors, contactors, filters, and safety devices.
Measure and record static pressure, refrigerant temperatures, superheat/subcool, temperature split, amp draws, voltage, and capacitor readings.
Test system performance and verify everything's running the way it should.
Catch worn or failing components before they turn into emergency calls.
Explain findings in plain language, backed by photos — no jargon, no games.
Recommend repairs based on what the system actually needs, never on pressure.
Educate homeowners on indoor air quality, comfort, and energy-saving solutions when they provide genuine value and improve system performance.
Introduce qualified homeowners to our maintenance membership program.
Flag replacement opportunities when a system's genuinely reached the end of the road.
Document every visit in ServiceTitan — photos, technician notes, equipment readings, diagnostic findings, and all recommendations to the homeowner.

Follow every safety policy and TDLR regulation, every time.
Perform all work in accordance with manufacturer specifications, local building codes, company quality standards, and all applicable safety policies.

EPA Section 608 Certification (required)
TDLR Registered or Certified HVAC Technician (required)
3-4 years of residential HVAC experience
Valid Texas driver's license with a clean driving record
Ability to lift 50+ lbs and work in attics and outdoor Texas heat

title: Solar Field Service Technician
description:
Solar Field Service Technician — Troubleshoot, Repair, Deliver.
Houston, TX  |  Full-Time  |  Hourly, Non-Exempt  |  Regional Travel
A solar system stops making sense the moment it stops making power. When that call comes in, you're the one who shows up, figures out what's wrong, and fixes it — on the spot.
Freedom Power was born when Freedom Solar and Freedom HVAC joined forces to become Texas's complete whole-house energy company. We don't just install equipment. We hand homeowners the keys to something bigger: control over their energy, their bills, and their future. We call it Energy Empowerment, and it's not a tagline — it's the reason we show up every day.
As a Solar Field Service Technician, you're the technical expert who keeps residential solar, storage, and off-grid systems running the way they're supposed to. You'll respond to dispatch calls, troubleshoot and diagnose issues, climb the roof when the job calls for it, and walk homeowners through exactly what you found and why — building trust one service call at a time.
Your Day-to-Day
Respond to service calls from dispatch on behalf of customers with solar system issues.
Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair Solar, storage, and off-grid systems.
Get on roofs when needed to remove, replace, or repair solar panels.
Deliver an exceptional customer experience on every visit.
Communicate findings clearly and follow procedures with your manager.
Handle paperwork, timekeeping, and inventory processing for every service call.
Collect payment for services rendered and identify legitimate upsell opportunities in the field.
Complete the job disposition form after every service call.
Take on other duties as assigned by the Service Operations Manager.
What You Bring
Prior solar installation experience
Valid Apprentice Electrician license (required)
OSHA 10 certification (required)
Valid driver's license and willingness to travel regionally, frequently
Solid knowledge of local electrical codes and residential PV design and components
Strong understanding of residential AC (microinverters) and DC (string & optimizer) PV systems
Thorough understanding of residential electrical systems and how to work safely around them
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, safely
Comfortable learning new technical and diagnostic skills as systems evolve
Able to withstand heights, climb ladders, and work outdoors in hot and cold conditions
The Physical Side
Comfortable with light lifting and carrying (under 15 lbs), straight pulling, and simple grasping
Able to walk, stand, and sit for extended periods
Comfortable operating office equipment and motor vehicles, with travel by car up to 10% of the time
Able to work independently as well as with others

Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
100% Company-Sponsored Short-Term Disability

Weekly Pay Dates
3 Weeks PTO + 3 Sick Days
12 Paid Holidays + 1 Floating Holiday
Real upward mobility — this role is a launchpad, not a ceiling

title: Operations Project Manager
description:

Location & Team Gatherings
 
Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016.  We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office - we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON.
 
We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture.


About This Role
As part of Intersect’s Operations team, you’ll lead the planning and coordination that enables high-impact operational projects across our fleet of solar, wind, battery energy storage, and gas assets. This role is focused on preparing complex, non-routine campaigns for successful execution by developing project plans, coordinating technical stakeholders, managing warranty-related activities, and ensuring operational readiness before work begins in the field.
 
Reporting to the Head of Operations, you'll serve as the organizational engine behind major capital improvements, fleet-wide campaigns, and warranty remediation projects. Team Overview
This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect’s mission to accelerate the clean energy transition by ensuring our operating fleet performs safely, reliably, and efficiently. Joining this team means helping solve complex technical challenges while contributing to projects that directly improve fleet performance, reliability, and long-term value.
 
What You'll Do
Drive Project Readiness
Lead upstream planning activities for major operational campaigns, systemic capital improvements, and specialized fleet-wide projects.
Develop detailed scopes of work, constructability reviews, engineering coordination, and project execution plans before field mobilization.
Build and maintain critical-path project schedules using tools such as Primavera P6, MS Project, or Smartsheet.
Deliver complete execution packages—including schedules, material plans, and safety requirements—to Site and Campus Managers for field execution.
 
Lead Warranty Operations & Commercial Recovery
Serve as the operational lead for complex OEM warranty campaigns across the operating fleet.
Coordinate technical documentation required to support warranty claims and commercial recovery efforts alongside the Asset Management team.
Review OEM repair methodologies, schedules, and execution plans to ensure they meet Intersect's technical and safety standards.
Establish processes to accurately track labor, equipment usage, downtime, and other costs that support warranty reimbursement and commercial claims.
 
Coordinate Outage Planning
Develop strategic pre-work plans for multi-unit outages and large operational campaigns.
Partner with the Integrated Operations Center (IOC) to coordinate curtailment windows, system isolations, and grid-related planning activities.
Collaborate with Central Planning to ensure specialized tools, materials, safety equipment, and long-lead components are available before project mobilization.
 
Maintain Project Controls & Data Integrity
Collect and organize as-built documentation, quality records, and project closeout packages following campaign completion.
Partner with CMMS Administration to ensure equipment updates, warranty records, and asset changes are accurately documented within Sitetracker.
Maintain accurate project controls, schedules, documentation, and reporting throughout the project lifecycle.
 
Collaborate Across Technical Teams
Build strong partnerships across Operations, Engineering, Asset Management, Planning, and external contractors.
Support consistent execution standards across multiple technologies and operating sites.
Identify planning risks early and develop mitigation strategies that improve project execution and operational outcomes.
 
What You'll Bring
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
3–6+ years of experience in technical project management, project controls, contract execution, or operations planning within utility-scale energy, power generation, or heavy industrial environments.
Experience developing critical-path schedules using Primavera P6, MS Project, Smartsheet, or similar scheduling software.
Strong understanding of project controls, planning methodologies, and complex operational project execution.
Experience working within contractual frameworks including OEM warranties, EPC agreements, TSAs, BSAs, or similar commercial agreements.
Ability to interpret technical documentation and coordinate engineering, commercial, and operational stakeholders.
Experience collecting documentation that supports commercial recovery, warranty reimbursement, or contractual claims.
Familiarity with one or more utility-scale technologies including solar, battery energy storage systems (BESS), wind, or gas generation assets.
Strong analytical, organizational, and documentation skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Comfortable managing multiple complex projects while balancing competing priorities.
Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
PMP certification is preferred.
CMRP certification is preferred.
A proactive, ownership-oriented mindset and a collaborative work style will help you succeed in this role.

description:

Silfab Solar is the North American leader in the design, development, and manufacture of high-efficiency, premium quality solar cells and solar modules. Silfab leverages more than 40 years of solar experience and best-in-class technologies operating state-of-the-art facilities in Burlington, Washington, Fort Mill, South Carolina and corporate headquarters in Toronto, Canada.  Each operating facility features multiple automated production lines, certified to the ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System standard, and just-in-time manufacturing to deliver Buy American approved PV modules specifically designed for and dedicated to the North American market. 

We are committed to investing in our employees, providing a dynamic and supportive environment for learning and professional growth.  We offer competitive pay, generous benefits, and opportunities for advancement, but more importantly, we offer you the ability to make a real difference in the world. 

 

Summary of Position 

As a Production Operator in Cell Manufacturing, you will operate your assigned station safely and efficiently to produce high-quality solar cells. Depending on your assignment, this may include loading wafers, operating print or testing equipment, inspecting and sorting cells, labeling, or packing finished product — always following the cleanroom, ESD, and contamination-control standards that protect fragile, high-value material. 

 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities 

  • Operate automatic and semi-automatic cell-manufacturing equipment according to station Standard Work Instructions (SWI). 
  • Follow all cleanroom gowning, ESD, and contamination-control requirements when handling wafers and cells. 
  • Load, handle, and move wafers, cells, cassettes, and magazines using correct technique to minimize breakage and contamination. 
  • Clean and prepare the workstation, equipment, and cassettes or tooling. 
  • Perform in-process quality checks and electrical or visual testing as required by the assigned station. 
  • Identify, mark, and segregate acceptable and defective wafers and cells. 
  • Check finished cells for correct labeling, packaging, and configuration. 
  • Record production, quality, and downtime information on the required station paperwork. 
  • Maintain compliance with established policies, procedures, and 5S standards. 
  • Complete other tasks as required and/or directed. 

Skills  

  • Hand-eye coordination, manual dexterity, and the ability to distinguish between colors. 
  • Ability to read, understand, and follow work instructions in English. 
  • Careful, consistent handling of fragile, high-value material. 
  • Basic computer literacy. 

Traits  

  • Coachable and willing to learn. 
  • Punctual and dependable 
  • Team and customer oriented. 
  • Attention to detail. 
  • Problem Solving.

Education and/or Experience

  • Production or manufacturing experience preferred; cleanroom experience an asset. 

Physical Requirements 

  • Must be able to lift and move materials up to 25 pounds independently and participate in team lifts of approximately 60 pounds as required for essential production tasks. 
  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position or move throughout the production floor for extended periods (for the duration of the shift up to 8+ hours per shift). 
  • Must be able to operate, position, adjust, or move equipment, tools, or materials necessary for production processes. 
  • Capable of performing consistent, manual production tasks over long shifts. 
  • Must be able to work in a gowned cleanroom and typical manufacturing environment, including required PPE and ESD controls, noise, and temperature variation. 
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Ability to work overtime and weekends when required.
  • Must be able to travel up to 50% of the time.

Purpose 

Support the advancement of utility-scale solar and BESS projects through all phases of electrical design by providing technical oversight, coordination, and review of electrical deliverables. Ensure electrical design quality, constructability, code compliance, and alignment with project scope, schedule, cost, customer requirements, and execution objectives. 

Responsibilities 

  • Lead the progression of electrical design from preliminary design through IFC and construction phases, ensuring deliverables are completed in sequence to support project schedules. 
  • Review and validate electrical design outputs, including conductor schedules, equipment specifications and layouts, monitoring and communication systems, grounding, string layouts, voltage drop calculations, and related electrical deliverables. 
  • Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for electrical design and constructability, including DC collection, AC collection, MV systems, equipment selection, grounding, monitoring, communications, and electrical code compliance. 
  • Provide technical guidance to internal teams, external engineering partners, vendors, and subcontractors. 
  • Collaborate with Engineering, Preconstruction, Estimating, Procurement, and Operations teams to align electrical design with project execution, procurement strategy, installation sequencing, and cost expectations.

  • Identify risks, gaps, and inconsistencies in electrical design packages and drive resolution with internal and external stakeholders. 
  • Evaluate electrical design decisions for constructability, installation efficiency, equipment availability, code compliance, customer requirements, and cost impacts. 
  • Interface with customers, developers, AHJs, external engineering firms, regulatory agencies, vendors, and subcontractors to align on electrical design approach, technical requirements, and compliance expectations. 
  • Support permitting and regulatory coordination by ensuring electrical designs comply with NEC requirements, customer specifications, jurisdictional requirements, and applicable standards. 
  • Provide technical support during construction, including review of field issues, design clarifications, RFI responses, change impacts, and resolution of electrical installation or constructability concerns. 
  • Manage and maintain project electrical files, drawings, documents, records, and design information in company systems. 
  • Support continuous improvement of electrical design processes, review standards, templates, and lessons learned to improve consistency, quality, and execution across utility-scale projects. 
  • Balance multiple complex projects and design priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy, accountability, and execution. 
  • Travel to project sites as needed to review existing conditions, support design coordination, assist with field issue resolution, and validate electrical systems or installation requirements.

title: Senior Substation Project Engineer
description: The Senior Substation Project Engineer is responsible for supporting the engineering, procurement, construction, testing, commissioning, and closeout of Substation electrical projects, with a primary focus on substations, transmission-related scopes, and interconnection facilities for utility-scale solar and battery energy storage projects. This role serves as a key technical and project execution interface between engineering, procurement, construction, subcontractors, consultants, utilities, and internal project stakeholders. The Project Engineer supports safe, cost-effective, schedule-driven, and technically compliant project delivery in accordance with contract requirements, applicable codes, utility standards, and PGS quality expectations. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: • Support the engineering execution of substations, transmission lines, gen-tie facilities, interconnection facilities, protection and controls systems, and related infrastructure from proposal state to project award through closeout. • Coordinate with internal engineering teams, external engineering consultants, procurement, construction, commissioning, and project management to ensure alignment on scope, schedule, budget, quality, and safety requirements. • Review engineering design packages, studies, drawings, specifications, calculations, equipment submittals, relay settings, protection and controls drawings, grounding designs, cable schedules, SCADA/communications drawings, and construction deliverables for completeness, constructability, and compliance with project requirements. • Support the development, review, and maintenance of project technical documentation, including design basis specifications, single-line diagrams, general arrangements, grounding plans, control schematics, wiring diagrams, equipment lists, test plans, commissioning documentation, and as-built records. • Assist in managing engineering deliverable schedules, consultant performance, design review cycles, comment resolution, and technical action items to support project milestones and construction readiness. • Track, log, and help resolve technical RFIs, design clarifications, field change requests, non-conformance items, and engineering support during construction, testing, commissioning, and energization. • Support procurement of long-lead Substation equipment, including transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, relays, control buildings, protection panels, station service equipment, battery systems, fiber/telecom equipment, and other substation materials. • Review vendor drawings, technical submittals, equipment data sheets, bills of material, factory test procedures, and operation and maintenance manuals for conformance with project specifications and utility requirements. • Participate in factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, equipment inspections, and resolution of technical issues with vendors, suppliers, and subcontractors. • Support construction teams by reviewing work plans, installation details, test results, turnover documentation, punch lists, and commissioning packages. • Assist with permitting, project planning, schedule development, progress tracking, cost forecasting, risk identification, and reporting related to engineering and technical scopes. • Support technical compliance with interconnection agreements, utility requirements, power purchase agreements, EPC contracts, owner specifications, permits, and applicable project documents. • Coordinate with utilities, independent engineers, owner’s engineers, AHJs, EPC partners, subcontractors, and consultants to resolve technical issues and support successful project execution. • Conduct technical evaluations, feasibility reviews, constructability reviews, value engineering assessments, and risk assessments for proposed Substation project scopes. • Support estimating, proposal development, EPC bid reviews, subcontractor evaluations, project handoff, and lessons learned activities by providing technical and execution-focused input. • Ensure designs and work activities comply with applicable codes and standards, including IEEE, ANSI, NESC, NEC, NFPA, OSHA, NEMA, IEC, utility standards, and project-specific requirements. • Support testing, commissioning, energization, and turnover activities, including coordination of test plans, commissioning checklists, relay testing documentation, outage planning, and utility witness requirements. • Lead and represent PGS in technical coordination meetings with consultants, engineering partners, and, as needed, clients and regulatory authorities. • Maintain accurate project records, design review logs, RFI logs, submittal logs, punch lists, commissioning documentation, lessons learned, and technical closeout packages. • Promote a culture of safety, quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and proactive communication across engineering and project execution teams. Education and/or Work Experience Requirements: Required • B.S. degree in Electrical, Civil, or Mechanical Engineering from an ABET-accredited university, or related technical discipline. • 5 to 10 years of experience in substation and/or transmission line engineering, design, or project engineering roles. • Working knowledge of applicable industry standards and codes, including IEEE, ANSI, NESC, NEC, and NEMA. • Demonstrated ability to review engineering deliverables produced by external consultants, EPC contractors, or engineering service providers, and to identify design errors, omissions, or non-conformances. • Represent PGS in technical coordination meetings with consultants, engineering partners, and, as needed, clients and regulatory authorities. • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to coordinate across engineering, project management, procurement, and construction disciplines. • Proficiency with the Microsoft Office suite, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and SharePoint. • Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, scaling organization. • Ability to travel occasionally, up to 15%, to project sites and factory acceptance test locations. Preferred • Engineer in Training (EIT) certification, with progress toward Professional Engineer (PE) licensure. • Familiarity with power system analysis software such as ETAP, PSCAD, or PSS/E. • Experience working with distributed, multi-firm, or offshore engineering teams. • Experience in solar, BESS, or broader renewable energy interconnection projects. • Experience with document control systems, data rooms, submittal management, RFI tracking, punch list tracking, and project closeout documentation. Physical Requirements/Work Environment: Work is performed in a combination of office and field environments, including active construction and substation sites. Must be able to sit, stand, bend, twist, and lift up to 20 pounds. May be exposed to weather elements when in the field. Ability to wear the full complement of required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Limited out-of-town travel may be required.

The position may be filled at different experience levels based on demonstrated competency, technical knowledge, electrical qualifications, and ability to work independently. Work involving energized equipment, medium-voltage systems, or switching may only be performed by personnel who are specifically trained, qualified, and authorized. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Perform work in accordance with OSHA requirements, NFPA 70E principles, applicable regulations, and Strata safety policies and procedures. Participate in effective job briefings, identify and communicate hazards, use required PPE, and exercise stop-work responsibility when unsafe conditions exist. Apply Lockout/Tagout, electrical isolation, and energized-work controls within the limits of individual training, qualification, and authorization. Perform scheduled and unscheduled preventive and corrective maintenance on BESS equipment and associated balance-of-plant systems. Inspect, maintain, troubleshoot, and support repair of battery systems, Power Conversion Systems, switchgear, transformers, auxiliary AC and DC systems, HVAC, fire detection and suppression interfaces, controls, protection systems, SCADA, networking, and communications equipment. Review alarms, event records, operating trends, and equipment status to identify abnormal conditions, isolate faults, and support safe restoration. Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical, controls, communications, and balance-of-plant issues using OEM diagnostic tools, technical documentation, monitoring systems, and electrical test equipment. Interpret single-line diagrams, schematics, wiring and control drawings, procedures, and OEM manuals to support maintenance and safe work planning. Use appropriate tools and test equipment, including multimeters, insulation-resistance testers, low-resistance ohmmeters, clamp meters, and thermal-imaging equipment. Verify repairs and document as-found and as-left equipment conditions before returning equipment to service. Write and perform switching orders when qualified and authorized under Strata’s switching program to establish electrical isolation boundaries and support safe restoration. Support commissioning, recommissioning, functional testing, point-to-point verification, system modifications, and punch-list resolution. Coordinate maintenance and troubleshooting activities with supervisors, Remote Operations, engineering, OEMs, vendors, contractors, utilities, and other support personnel. Support vendor and contractor field activities, including work-area coordination, safety alignment, scope verification, and collection of service and closeout documentation. Maintain accurate and timely CMMS records, including work orders, inspection results, test records, photographs, material usage, corrective actions, and equipment status. Collect technical information required for warranty claims, engineering review, recurring-failure analysis, and contractual reporting. Maintain assigned tools, test equipment, spare parts, materials, and company property in serviceable condition. Provide task guidance and technical support to less-experienced technicians or contractors when assigned and qualified. Support emergency response and Emergency Action Plan activities within assigned training and responsibilities. Maintain site readiness, equipment-area cleanliness, and housekeeping. Participate in on-call coverage and travel to other operating facilities as required. Perform other duties as assigned. seoDescription:
Rosendin Electric, one of the largest electrical contractors in the United States, seeks an Estimator II for its El Paso, TX office. This mid-level position involves preparing bid documents and cost estimates for electrical construction projects, with support from senior estimators on small- to medium-sized assignments. The role offers hands-on experience in takeoff calculations, supplier coordination, and project handoff meetings with field teams.

Responsibilities

  • Review proposal specifications and drawings to determine scope of work and bidding requirements
  • Prepare detailed estimates by calculating complete takeoffs and entering data into the estimating system; verify accuracy and completeness of printouts
  • Identify and solicit quotes from qualified suppliers and subcontractors; review quotes for compliance with plans and specifications
  • Quantify and itemize all bid components, including subcontract work, equipment rental, tools, and supplies
  • Assist in developing labor productivity and installation unit costs based on site conditions and historical data
  • Compile scope of work, technical requirements, and pricing; present bid packages to Lead Estimator, Estimating Manager, and Chief Estimator
  • Meet with project management and senior estimators at project turnover to explain estimate details, scope, quotes, and transition considerations
  • Prepare scope letter inclusions, exclusions, and clarifications
  • Ensure timely completion of all client-required documents and maintain supporting files for estimating assumptions

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or related field (or combination of education, training, and relevant experience)
  • Minimum 3 years of experience estimating data centers and/or commercial construction projects, preferably electrical
  • Proficiency in Accubid estimating software
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering design drawings, specifications, and front-end documents
  • Proficiency in CAD or 3D software (preferred)
  • Advanced knowledge of construction technology, estimating techniques, and cost control
  • Competency with computerized cost data systems and electrical systems
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel)
  • Capacity to perform arithmetic calculations and work under time pressure
  • Ability to lift occasionally up to 30 lbs
  • Up to 10% travel

  • 401(k) with company match
  • Annual performance-based bonus
  • 17 PTO days plus 10 paid holidays annually
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Term life, AD&D, and voluntary life insurance
  • Disability income protection
  • Pre-tax flexible spending accounts (health and dependent care)

seoDescription:
SOLV Energy seeks a Project Manager to oversee high-voltage substation construction, testing, and energization on utility-scale solar and battery storage projects nationwide. This fully remote role manages the complete substation lifecycle—from design review and procurement through commissioning—coordinating engineering, construction, and utility stakeholders to ensure on-time, on-budget delivery of 69kV to 500kV infrastructure.

Responsibilities

  • Execute project engineering duties with emphasis on substation design, construction, testing, and energization
  • Review Power Purchase Agreements, Generator Interconnection Agreements, Utility Interconnection Requirements, contract documents, System Impact Studies, Facility Studies, and Owner/Engineer specifications for substation scope compliance
  • Oversee LNTP and early-stage deliverables for HV and substation workstreams, ensuring alignment with permitting and utility timelines
  • Develop, manage, and track substation budgets including primary equipment procurement, civil sitework, grounding systems, protection and control, SCADA integration, and construction labor
  • Create detailed subcontractor scopes of work for substation EPC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction) including testing and commissioning
  • Lead and manage substation subcontractors through RFI coordination, billing reviews, change orders, daily reporting, safety performance, and schedule tracking
  • Monitor and control substation scope changes and associated commercial impacts
  • Facilitate Project Kick-Off Meetings, site Kick-Off Meetings, Pre-Commissioning Walks, and Energization Readiness Reviews with dedicated focus on substation milestones and risks
  • Manage RFIs and submittals relevant to substation scope, coordinating resolution with engineering and construction teams
  • Lead Utility Coordination Meetings focused on relay settings, protection schemes, testing protocols, switching orders, and interconnection management
  • Participate in Owner Coordination Meetings to communicate substation progress, risks, and technical issues
  • Engage in system engineering team meetings to coordinate interdependencies between PV, BESS, and substation infrastructure
  • Oversee procurement of long-lead substation components including power transformers, breakers, steel structures, control enclosures, relays, and communication systems
  • Facilitate construction schedule and scope review meetings, identifying critical paths for substation construction and energization
  • Coordinate PV and substation energization support including relay testing, functional checkouts, and utility witness testing
  • Manage Final Completion Punchlist for all substation work and documentation including redlines, test reports, as-builts, relay settings, and regulatory compliance records
  • Ensure safe work environment and enforce safety practices around energized substations and high-voltage equipment
  • Maintain flexible availability for substation construction and commissioning events outside regular business hours
  • Travel regularly to project sites, utility offices, and vendor facilities
  • Support continuous improvement, lessons learned, and standardization efforts across substation projects

Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in substation design, construction, or commissioning of utility-scale or industrial high-voltage systems (69kV to 500kV)
  • Demonstrated experience working on projects in the Northeast Region of the United States
  • Proven ability to manage multi-disciplinary substation projects through full lifecycle from kickoff to energization
  • Familiarity with substation components: power transformers, circuit breakers, switchgear, grounding systems, control buildings, protection and control systems, relays, and SCADA
  • Experience managing transmission line construction projects
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Project Management Professional (PMP) certification preferred
  • NFPA 70E "Qualified Person" certification preferred; must demonstrate familiarity with energized work practices and LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) protocols
  • Working knowledge of utility operations, switching procedures, relay testing, and energization protocols
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Primavera P6 scheduling experience preferred
  • Experience with CAD, PDF markup tools, and field documentation platforms a plus
  • Ability to frequently walk, bend, stand, and lift 20+ pounds on uneven terrain at construction sites
  • Ability to visually inspect and verify HV equipment installations, conduct site walks, and observe electrical testing safely
  • Occasional climbing, working at heights, or accessing substation steel platforms required
  • Ability to work in outdoor environments and in proximity to energized equipment
  • Compliance with all site-specific PPE and safety training requirements
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States without requiring employer sponsorship

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Basic life and disability insurance
  • 401(k) plan enrollment
  • Vacation, sick, and holiday pay
  • Salary range: $110,837–$138,547 annually

seoDescription:
Primoris Renewable Energy is hiring an Electrician for the Desert Pine BESS project in Louisiana. The role centers on electrical installation, maintenance, and repair at a large-scale battery energy storage facility. Work involves systems such as batteries, inverters, transformers, and switchgear in a construction setting.

Responsibilities

  • Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures according to blueprints, schematics, and applicable electrical codes.
  • Conduct routine inspections, troubleshooting, and preventive maintenance on BESS electrical systems including batteries, inverters, transformers, and switchgear.
  • Diagnose and correct electrical malfunctions using testing devices and tools.
  • Connect electrical power to equipment while following grounding and safety protocols.
  • Follow all safety regulations and company policies, including Lockout/Tagout procedures.
  • Coordinate with project managers, engineers, and other trades to support project timelines.
  • Record details of repairs, installations, and maintenance activities.
  • Operate and maintain electrical tools and equipment.
  • Provide training and supervision to apprentice electricians when required.

Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent; completion of an accredited electrician apprenticeship program preferred.
  • Valid Journeyman Electrician license for the relevant jurisdiction.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years of experience as a qualified electrician, with preference for renewable energy, industrial, or utility settings.
  • Knowledge of electrical theory, principles, and practices including AC/DC circuits, control systems, and power distribution.
  • Experience with battery energy storage systems or large-scale electrical infrastructure preferred.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical blueprints, schematics, and technical manuals.
  • Understanding of the National Electrical Code and relevant local electrical codes.
  • Capability to lift heavy objects, climb ladders, and work in various weather conditions.
  • OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification preferred.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

This role prepares bid and submittal documents along with cost estimates for electrical construction projects and serves as lead estimator, coordinating with other estimators, suppliers, and customers. We train you to work across different teams—from qualifying homes for solar, to installing, to inspecting the final work, and servicing existing systems. This versatility helps limit reduced hours and ehances job security in an industry affected by seasons. It also means you can solve customer problems in one visit, keeping you safely off the road and moving your career forward. Competitive hourly base pay and lucrative performance incentives through our Nike/Carhartt Sponsored incentive program, The League.
